newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: IMF, Zimbabwe to hold key aid talks next month.
newsitem.headline: IMF, Zimbabwe to hold key aid talks next month.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is due to hold crucial talks with Zimbabwe next month which could determine Western donors' support for an economic reform plan due to begin later this year.

At his first press briefing since assuming office in the southern African state two weeks ago, new IMF resident representative Robert Franco said a Fund mission was expected in Harare at the end of October for talks focusing on Zimbabwe's plans to tackle its crippling budget deficit.
"We are hoping a mission will come here probably towards the end of October," Franco said.

The IMF and the World Bank -- which helped marshall Western donor support for Zimbabwe's first five-year economic structural adjustment programme (ESAP) which ended last year -- withheld some aid in mid 1995 when President Robert Mugabe's government failed to implement a series of cost saving measures.

The two organisations and other key donors say big government spending -- which currently accounts for about 40 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) and contributed to a 10.1 percent budget deficit in the last financial year -- is fuelling inflation and stifling economic growth by keeping interest rates high.
In the past two years, annual inflation has averaged 22 percent while interest rates averaged 24 percent.

Mugabe's government says it hopes to bring down inflation to 17 percent, interest rates to below 20 percent and the budget deficit to around eight percent by the end of the current fiscal year in June 1997.
Franco reaffirmed that the IMF's support for further reforms would depend on Zimbabwe's efforts to restore macro-economic stability by reducing spending and the budget deficit.
Other Western donors say their positions would be determined based on the IMF and the World Bank's stance.
The IMF representative said he would not comment on Zimbabwe's current budget until it had been debated by parliament and formally dicussed by the IMF and the government.

Zimbabwe's Finance Minister Herbert Murerwa is due to hold initial talks with IMF officials -- including managing director Michel Camdessus -- early next month in Washington during the IMF/World Bank annual meetings before the Harare discussions.
"We have planned that they meet (IMF) managing director Michel Camdessus and hold preliminary discussions with other staff," he said.

"But we have to be prepared to think about possible solutions (to Zimbabwe's budgetary problems) because it will be unfortunate if the mission comes and we have not prepared ourselves to be able to hold fruitful discussions," he added.
Franco said it was crucial for Zimbabwe to tackle the budget problems to be able to achieve sustainable GDP growth.
Zimbabwe hopes to post seven percent GDP growth this year after it shrunk by about two percent in 1995.
